subject: Reserved capacity pricing sensitivity — runway, discount ask, and exec signer
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@peridot.ai>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity pricing sensitivity — initial proposal and ask

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Attached is a short model of how Peridot's committed reserved capacity (12-month, 1.2M token-hours/month) maps to our expected GPU cost exposure under three market scenarios: base, +20% GPU cost spike, and +40% extreme. The key pieces for your finance team are in the left tab (runway / burn by month) and the right tab shows the discount ladder we can offer at different commit bands.

Quick summary:
- Base case: effective unit price = $0.014/token-hour with a 20% commit discount (shown in Term Sheet v2).
- +20% GPU cost: we absorb some cost through burst credits and a temporary 6% marginal concession (see row 24).
- +40% GPU cost: we need an executive-level approval to make a one-time rebate/credit; without that our effective pass-through would exceed the committed discount band and we'd need to reprice.

Ask: can you confirm whether Peridot can accept (A) a 60/40 payment cadence (monthly w/ 40% holdback at quarter end), and (B) an executive approval path for a one-time rebate up to 5% of the committed spend if GPU spot costs exceed +35% for >30 days? If Peridot cannot sign for an exec-signer statement, we need to propose an alternative: a dynamic indexation clause tied to the GPU price index (example in the Term Sheet v2).

I've looped in Kimberly (pricing) and David (finance/ops) to validate our internal ask and make sure we can operationalize the rebate without breaking our ledger. Marcus — if you can review the attached runway model and highlight any ops constraints on the rebate flow, that would be very helpful.

Attachments: peridot_reserved_model_runway.xlsx (xlsx), proposed_term_sheet_v2.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@peridot.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts@peridot.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity pricing sensitivity — initial proposal and ask

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the model and clear write-up. I reviewed with our CFO and procurement lead this morning. A couple quick points: we like the 12-month tenor and the tiered discount structure, but we don't have an internal exec-signer authorization to accept an open-ended rebate clause tied to vendor GPU markets. Procurement recommended either: (1) a capped contingency credit (your suggested one-time rebate up to 5%), or (2) an indexation clause with a clearly defined floor/ceiling and a quarterly reconciliation.

On cadence: the 60/40 payment cadence is doable but we'd prefer the 40% holdback to be released within 30 days of quarter close rather than 60 — can you confirm if that aligns with your revenue recognition/ops?

We also asked finance to review the XLS and will come back with a small list of line-item questions by Friday.

—Sarah
Sarah Mills
Head of Platform Partnerships, Peridot AI
sarah.mills@peridot.ai

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity pricing sensitivity — runway and accounting implications

Jasmine / team —

Reviewed the runway doc and the proposed term sheet. Two internal notes:

1) Revenue recognition & holdback: The 60/40 cadence with 40% holdback is workable if Peridot agrees to a 30-day release after quarter close (that matches their ask) AND we capture a service-level milestone to avoid recognition ambiguity. We should add a clause in the term sheet: "holdback release contingent on usage reconciliation and SLA threshold (>=98% uptime)".

2) Rebate mechanics: We can support a capped contingency credit of up to 5% of committed spend for the year, but approval must come from Finance + Head of Partnerships (Marcus) because this will be posted as contra-revenue and affects monthly MRR calculations. Operationally we can process a credit as a one-off invoice adjustment; the runway model needs a credit line for month-of-impact and a note about tax treatment.

Marcus — please confirm you can sign for the rebate cap approval or suggest routing to an exec approver. If Marcus signs, we can pre-authorize Legal to finalize language in Term Sheet v3.

Kimberly Park
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@peridot.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity pricing sensitivity — runway, routing, and sign-off

All —

I reviewed the attachments and Kimberly's notes. I am prepared to approve a capped contingency credit up to 5% of the first-year committed spend for PRD-4872, provided we get:

- A clear trigger definition: GPU spot index > +35% for 30 consecutive days (index source: CloudGPU Spot Index — linked in the term sheet).
- A single redemption mechanism: credit applied to the next invoice after reconciliation (no retroactive cash payout).
- Legal-approved language that limits credits to committed months only and excludes burst/overage usage.
- A clear communications plan with Peridot that we will publish a one-line accounting footnote for the credit.

Jasmine — please update Term Sheet v2 into v3 to reflect the capped credit and the 30-day holdback release, then route to Legal (copy me). Sarah — if Peridot can sign v3 with the language above, we can proceed to DocuSign; I will be the internal signer for the rebate cap.

Marcus Lin
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
